evidence: Lazorec, arXiv:2405.04141, primary paper on extraspecial and generalized/almost extraspecial groups.
correctness.rationale: The matrix multiplication law gives the commutator \(g(0,0,ab'+a'b)\), so the derived subgroup and center are exactly the central coordinate subgroup. In characteristic two, \(g(a,b,c)^2=g(0,0,ab)\), and every central coordinate is a square, hence \(H'=Z=\Phi\). A nonidentity element has order two exactly when \(ab=0\); counting those pairs gives \(2q^2-q-1\), and every remaining element has order four. The resulting sum-of-orders formula follows algebraically. A fresh independent \(q=4\) replay gave order counts \(1,27,36\) and total \(199\), matching the formula.
risks: The finite replay is corroborative only; the all-field statement rests on the symbolic group-law calculation.
